findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header is missing
findings.description: A Content-Security-Policy limits where scripts and other resources can load from and reduces the impact of cross-site scripting.
findings.evidence: Content-Security-Policy was not present. Checked the HTTP 200 response from https://example.com/. Security headers seen: strict-transport-security: max-age=300; x-content-type-options: nosniff; referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin; permissions-policy: camera=(), microphone=().
findings.remediation: Define a CSP that restricts script sources, e.g. start in report-only mode with "default-src 'self'" and tighten from there.

findings.title: Cookies set without the HttpOnly attribute
findings.description: Cookies without HttpOnly are readable by scripts, so a cross-site scripting flaw could steal them. This matters most for session cookies.
findings.remediation: Add HttpOnly to cookies that scripts do not need to read, especially session cookies.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security max-age is short
findings.description: A short HSTS lifetime reduces how long browsers enforce HTTPS.
findings.remediation: Use a max-age of at least 15552000 seconds (180 days); 1 year is common.

findings.title: No security.txt contact file
findings.description: A security.txt file (RFC 9116) tells researchers how to report a vulnerability to you. Without one, reports may not reach the right person.
findings.evidence: GET https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt returned HTTP 404 without a valid Contact field.
findings.remediation: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with at least a Contact line and an Expires date, for example: Contact: mailto:security@your-domain
